newsitem.title: USA: Blue Cross to merge operations in Md., Va. area.
newsitem.headline: Blue Cross to merge operations in Md., Va. area.

text.p: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Maryland (BCBSM) and Blue Cross and Blue Shield of the National Capital Area (BCBSNCA) said they plan to merge operations under a new holding company.

The combined companies, with a total workforce of 5,000 and more than $3 billion in annual revenues, would serve more than two million members in Maryland, Washington, D.C. and Northern Virginia, they said.
Details of the transaction would be finalized in a formal, definitive agreement, pending requisite regulatory approvals, they said.
Under the proposal, the two plans would be subsidiaries of a yet-to-be named holding company governed by a board of directors made up of directors from the existing boards of both plans.
William L. Jews, president and chief executive of the Maryland Blue Cross, would become president and chief executive of the new holding company.
Larry Glasscock, president and chief exeuctive of the National Capital Area plan, would serve as the chief operating officer.
Jews would serve as chairman of the two plans and Glasscock as president and chief executive officer.
No changes are anticipated in the locations of any of the key operating units for either of the two plans or their subsidiaries.

Combined, the companies cover the health care needs of nearly 528,000 federal workers and their families and have the largest membership among the 61 Blues plans in the Federal Employee Program (FEP) in 1996.

BCBSM and BCBSNCA experienced significant growth in enrollment in 1996, adding nearly 80,000 members to their combined rolls. BCBSNCA has more than 760,000 members in the Washington metropolitan area while BCBSM serves more than 1.39 million Maryland residents.
Last year, BCBSM and BCBSNCA announced an agreement to jointly market a Medicare Risk product and to jointly administer claims of large regional and national employer accounts.
